_readme: Every number the game uses lives here so non-coders can balance the game. 'nasa' entries are real-world values with a source; 'game' entries are design choices built from them. Rounded for 10-15 year olds.

o2PerAstronautKg.unit: kg per crew member per day
o2PerAstronautKg.label: Oxygen breathed by one astronaut
o2PerAstronautKg.source: NASA Life Support Baseline Values and Assumptions Document (BVAD), NASA/TP-2015-218570/REV1

waterPerAstronautKg.unit: kg per crew member per day
waterPerAstronautKg.label: Drinking water + water in food for one astronaut

foodPerAstronautKg.unit: kg per crew member per day (packaged)
foodPerAstronautKg.label: Packaged food for one astronaut

waterRecovery.label: Water the ISS life-support system can recycle
waterRecovery.source: NASA: ISS Environmental Control and Life Support System reached 98% water recovery (June 2023)

marsSunlight.label: Sunlight reaching Mars (Mars is about 1.5x farther from the Sun)
marsSunlight.source: NASA Mars Fact Sheet: solar irradiance 586 W/m2 at Mars vs 1361 W/m2 at Earth

marsDoseMsvPerDay.label: Radiation dose on the surface of Mars (cosmic rays)
marsDoseMsvPerDay.source: Curiosity RAD instrument, Hassler et al., Science 343 (2014); NASA/JPL

moonDoseMsvPerDay.label: Radiation dose on the surface of the Moon (cosmic rays)
moonDoseMsvPerDay.source: Chang'e-4 Lunar Lander Neutrons and Dosimetry (LND), Zhang et al., Science Advances 6 (2020): 1,369 microSv/day

careerDoseLimitMsv.label: NASA career radiation limit for astronauts
careerDoseLimitMsv.source: NASA-STD-3001 Vol. 1 (2022 update): 600 mSv career effective dose limit

lunarNightDays.label: Length of a night at most places on the Moon
lunarNightDays.source: NASA Moon facts; LRO illumination maps show some south-pole rims are lit most of the time

kilopowerKwe.label: Small fission reactor power (Kilopower designs: 1 to 10 kWe)
kilopowerKwe.source: NASA Kilopower / KRUSTY test (2018) and Fission Surface Power project

moxieGramsPerHour.unit: grams of O2 per hour (best run)
moxieGramsPerHour.label: Oxygen made from Martian air by MOXIE on Perseverance
moxieGramsPerHour.source: NASA/JPL: MOXIE completes Mars mission (Sept 2023), 122 g total, up to 12 g/hour

game.doseLimitNote: One-twelfth of NASA's 600 mSv career limit, so one month on the surface can't use up more than a fair share.

crops._note: Growth times are sped up for a 30-sol game. Real growth times are in 'realDays'.

mixed.name: Salad + potato mix
mixed.fact: A mixed garden spreads the risk: if one crop fails, the others still feed the crew.

lettuce.name: Red romaine lettuce
lettuce.fact: In August 2015 ISS astronauts ate the first lettuce grown in space: 'Outredgeous' red romaine from NASA's Veggie unit. Fast and great for morale, but low in calories.

potato.name: Potatoes
potato.fact: NASA's Biomass Production Chamber at Kennedy Space Center grew potatoes, wheat, soybeans and lettuce for future bases. Potatoes give lots of calories per square metre, but take a long time.
potato.source: NASA Technical Reports: Biomass Production Chamber

wheat.name: Dwarf wheat
wheat.fact: 'USU-Apogee' dwarf wheat was bred with NASA support to grow short and fast under lamps, so it fits in a small space greenhouse.

soybean.name: Soybeans
soybean.fact: Soybeans are rich in protein and oil, so a base diet does not depend only on packaged food. NASA studied them in the Biomass Production Chamber.
soybean.source: NASA Technical Reports: Biomass Production Chamber

moon.name: Moon
moon.turnNote: On the Moon each turn is one Earth day.
moon.reactorNote: A 1 kWe Kilopower-class fission reactor running all day = 24 kWh, sun or no sun.
moon.arrayNote: Sunlight at the Moon is as strong as at Earth, but at the pole it comes in sideways, so panels stand upright and turn with the Sun.
moon.lesson: Store energy and shield the hab.
facts: No air: higher radiation and micrometeoroids reach the ground.
Some south-pole crater rims are sunny most of the time, but shadows still pass.
Ice in shadowed craters nearby can be mined for water.
Help from Earth is about 3 days away.

mars.name: Mars
mars.turnNote: On Mars each turn is one sol: 24 hours 39 minutes.
mars.reactorNote: No reactor yet: this base runs on sunlight and batteries, like the Opportunity rover did.
mars.arrayNote: Mars gets only 43% of Earth's sunlight, so this base brings a huge solar array: on a clear sol it makes 50 kWh.
facts: Weaker sunlight, and dust storms can block most of it.
Thin air gives a little protection from radiation.
CO2 in the air can be turned into oxygen (MOXIE proved it).
Help from Earth is months away.
